verdicts.quote: readBytes() at line 83-95 reads a 32-bit length prefix from untrusted network input via in.readInt(), sign-extends it to a long via unsignedExtend(), and allocates a byte array of that size.
verdicts.why: Exactly the mechanism: an attacker-declared length prefix sizes the buffer and the array is allocated on the strength of that number alone, before the payload bytes are shown to be present.

verdicts.quote: There is no recursion depth limit or stack depth check anywhere in this chain.
verdicts.why: F01 names the cycle readFieldValue -> readTable/readArray -> readFieldValue with no depth counter, so attacker-controlled nesting sets the recursion depth.
